records.text: Harmeet Dhillon transferred her stake in Dhillon Law Group to her brother, serves as assistant attorney general for the Civil Rights Division, and is the front-runner to replace Pam Bondi as attorney general.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: She left her firm, obviously, to go fill this position and I think transferred the stake in her in the company to her brother while she's currently serving in the Department of Justice. ... She's serving as the assistant attorney general for the Civil Rights Division. She's also the front runner to replace Pam Bondi for attorney general of the United States.

verification.notes: DOJ confirms Harmeet Dhillon has served as Assistant Attorney General for Civil Rights since April 2025. Her ethics disclosure said she intended to sell her Dhillon Law Group shares to her non-equity law partner and brother, but the reviewed record does not independently confirm completion of the transfer. At the relevant time, reporting described Dhillon as one of several names urged by supporters; Axios and other coverage identified Lee Zeldin and Todd Blanche, not Dhillon, as the leading candidates. The compound statement is partly true and partly overstated.
